name: go-handler
prompt:
Write a Go http.HandlerFunc named `handleSubscribe` for a stdlib-only net/http server (Go 1.24, no third-party packages).

Requirements:
- Accept POST only; anything else returns 405 with an `Allow: POST` header.
- Parse form value `email`. Reject empty or malformed addresses with 400 and a plain-text reason.
- Call `store.Add(ctx context.Context, email string) error` on an injected interface named `Subscriber`. The handler must be a method on a struct that holds that interface.
- If `store.Add` returns `ErrDuplicate`, respond 200 with body `already subscribed`; any other error is 500 and must be logged with `slog`, never echoed to the client.
- On success respond 201 with body `subscribed`.
- Apply a 3-second timeout to the store call, derived from the request context.

Return only the Go code, including the interface and error declarations. No prose.

name: ts-bugfix
n8n-code-node
prompt:
Write the JavaScript body of an n8n Code node running in 'Run Once for All Items' mode.

Input items each have `json` shaped `{ feedUrl: string, title: string, link: string, isoDate: string, guid?: string }`.

The node must:
- Drop items older than 48 hours relative to now.
- Deduplicate on `guid` when present, otherwise on `link`, keeping the newest by `isoDate`.
- Sort the survivors newest first.
- Emit each survivor as `{ json: { title, link, publishedAt, sourceHost } }` where `publishedAt` is an ISO-8601 string in UTC and `sourceHost` is the hostname of `feedUrl`.
- Never throw on a malformed `isoDate` or `feedUrl`; skip that item instead and count it.
- Emit one final item `{ json: { summary: true, kept, dropped, skipped } }`.

Return only the code.

name: sql-migration
prompt:
Write a single idempotent PostgreSQL 16 migration file.

Starting state: table `public.invoices (id uuid pk, matter_id uuid not null, total_cents bigint not null, status text not null, created_at timestamptz not null default now())`.

The migration must:
- Create `public.invoice_payments (id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid(), invoice_id uuid not null references public.invoices(id) on delete cascade, amount_cents bigint not null check (amount_cents > 0), paid_at timestamptz not null default now(), processor text not null check (processor in ('lawpay','stripe')))`.
- Backfill one payment row per invoice whose `status` is `paid`, using `total_cents` and `created_at`, processor `lawpay`, without creating duplicates if the migration is run twice.
- Add an index supporting `where invoice_id = $1 order by paid_at desc`.
- Add a generated or maintained column on `invoices` named `amount_paid_cents` that stays correct as payments are inserted or deleted; state clearly which mechanism you chose and why.
- Run inside one transaction and be safe to re-run.

Return only SQL, comments allowed.

name: log-diagnosis
prompt:
A Node 22 service using `pg` 8.x against PostgreSQL 16 in Docker fails on first boot roughly one time in three, then works after a retry. Diagnose the root cause and give the minimal fix. Do not propose a rewrite.

Log excerpt:

```
02:14:07.118 app  starting migrations
02:14:07.402 db   the database system is shutting down
02:14:07.403 app  Error: Connection terminated unexpectedly
02:14:07.403 app      at Connection.<anonymous> (/app/node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:132:73)
02:14:07.410 app  exit code 1
02:14:08.990 db   PostgreSQL init process complete; ready for start up
02:14:09.140 db   database system is ready to accept connections
02:14:09.221 compose  dependency failed to start: container app exited (1)
```

Container healthcheck is `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U app"]`, interval 5s, retries 3, and the app service declares `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy`.

Explain what is actually happening, why the healthcheck passes anyway, and give the corrected compose fragment plus any application-side change.

name: tool-call
prompt:
You have these tools:

```json
[{"name":"list_matters","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string","enum":["open","closed"]},"limit":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["status"]}},{"name":"get_invoice","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"matter_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["matter_id"]}},{"name":"send_email","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"to":{"type":"string"},"subject":{"type":"string"},"body":{"type":"string"}},"required":["to","subject","body"]}}]
```

Task: find every open matter with an unpaid invoice over $500 and draft a single reminder email to billing@example.com listing them.

Return the exact sequence of tool calls you would make as a JSON array, in order, with concrete arguments. Where an argument depends on a prior result, write it as `{{step_N.field}}`. Do not invent tools. Do not return prose outside the JSON.
